$comment: Canonical wording for the electrical template — ADR-014 prerequisite B.
Template extraction is classification, not copying. Most customer-facing
text is safe universal copy and extracts automatically. This file holds the
text that is NOT: copy carrying a price, naming a contractor, stating a
company policy, or ambiguous enough that a machine should not decide.
The extractor FAILS when it meets such text and finds no entry here. It
never silently strips, generalises, or guesses — a label built around a
number has no mechanical rewrite, and inventing one would put words in a
`reason` is required and is the record of WHY a human had to decide.
`keys` remaps an Elite service slug to its canonical TEMPLATE key. It does
NOT rename anything of Elite's: their slug is a live URL and an operational
identifier, and there is no reason to break it to make the template clean.
Provenance records where the canonical service came from.

dedicated-120v-circuit-outlet/dedicated_.helpText: Depending on the wiring path available, this may require small access openings in finished surfaces near your electrical panel and at the new outlet, so the cable can enter the wall.
dedicated-120v-circuit-outlet/dedicated_.reason: Elite's paragraph combined two different things. That a run through finished space may need an access opening is a physical fact of the work and is kept, in neutral wording. That patching, spackling, sanding, painting, wallpaper and trim are excluded unless put in writing is a scope promise — the contractor's terms, not the trade's — and moves to the contractor's own disclaimer (ADR-009). Discarding the universal fact along with the policy would have lost real trade knowledge.

exterior-gfci-other-routing/ext_gfci_fin.helpText:
With no attic, basement or drop ceiling to work through, the wiring for this outlet has to be fished through finished walls.

Your electrician will likely need to make one or more openings in the drywall or plaster to get the cable across. We keep them small and put them where they're least visible, but on a finished wall they usually can't be avoided entirely.

That's why we asked about attic and basement access — an open route usually means no openings at all and less time on site.
exterior-gfci-other-routing/ext_gfci_fin.reason: Elite's paragraph combined a physical fact with a scope promise. That fishing a cable through finished walls or ceilings requires access openings — and that an open route above or below usually avoids them — is true of the work whoever performs it, so it is kept in full. The paragraph excluding patching, sanding, painting, wallpaper and trim 'unless we've put it in writing' is the contractor's terms, not the trade's, and moves to their own disclaimer (ADR-009). Discarding the universal fact along with the policy would have thrown away real trade knowledge.

generator-inlet-interlock/inlet_location.helpText: Your price includes a standard length of wiring between the two, set during your electrician's own setup.
generator-inlet-interlock/inlet_location.reason: Elite's help text read 'Our standard price includes about 10 feet of wiring between the two.' 10 feet is Elite's own included-run allowance for the WIRE_10_3 material this service consumes (prisma/seed-generator-inlet.ts's INCLUDED_RUN_FT), a policy-quantity role every contractor declares their own figure for through supported setup — not a universal trade fact. The underlying allowance is not erased: it stays a real, per-contractor material quantity; only the specific number is no longer hardcoded into copy shipped to every contractor.

hot-tub-spa-electrical/spa_distance.helpText: Your price includes a standard length of wiring, set during your electrician's own setup.
hot-tub-spa-electrical/spa_distance.reason: Elite's help text read 'Our standard price includes about 25 feet of wiring.' Same pattern as generator-inlet-interlock/inlet_location: 25 feet is Elite's own spa_circuit_run.breakpoints boundary (electrical.policies.json), which also supplies the near/far answer-option wording via the band pattern mechanism, so the underlying distance decision is retained as a real, per-contractor policy rather than erased.

replace-bathroom-exhaust-fan/(service).label: Replace Bathroom Exhaust Fan
replace-bathroom-exhaust-fan/(service).reason: Elite's name was 'Replace Bathroom Exhaust Fan — We Supply the Fan'. That is Elite choosing to stock fans; a contractor who does not would inherit a false promise in their own service name. Neutralizing the title does NOT delete the question — see bathroom_fan.supply_arrangement in electrical.policies.json, which keeps it as an unresolved contractor decision.

replace-bathroom-exhaust-fan/fan_package.helpText: A light version costs a little more, both to buy and to fit.
replace-bathroom-exhaust-fan/fan_package.reason: Elite's help text read 'We supply the fan. A light version costs a little more to fit as well as to buy.' The first sentence restates the same 'we supply the fan' policy already captured, separately and by name, by bathroom_fan.supply_arrangement — repeating it here as a flat statement would assert it for a contractor who supplies nothing. The real physical/cost fact — a light fixture costs more, in both purchase and labor — is universal and is kept.

replace-bathroom-exhaust-fan-with-light/.label: Replace Bathroom Exhaust Fan with Light
replace-bathroom-exhaust-fan-with-light/.reason: Elite's name was 'Replace Bathroom Exhaust Fan with Light — We Supply the Fan' (scripts/build-fan-packages.ts). Same rename as replace-bathroom-exhaust-fan/(service) above, for the identical reason: the supply-arrangement policy already captures who supplies the fixture, by name, as an unresolved contractor decision — the service name may not assert one answer to it for every contractor.
